sources_reopened.note: 295 community-dwelling, SMMSE 1.9 (MCID 1.4), BADLS 3.0 (MCID 3.5) confirmed. Authors: cognitive benefits exceeded MCID.

Post hoc first-year analysis, HR 2.09 and no difference in next 3 years, England and Scotland, irreversible move confirmed. The absolute 0.20 and 0.37 are full-text figures; no PMC copy and Scite quota exhausted, so not re-read.
204, 26 UK centres, 12-week null, 7 vs 1 deaths by week 16, post hoc p=0.065 confirmed.
Mood stabilisers named as valproic acid and carbamazepine; gabapentin not in abstract; mood stabilisers already rising before programme; 2009 to 2014 US long-term care.
475, large effect d 0.97, maintained at 9 months, no significant secondary differences, blinded researchers confirmed.
Mean change 2.57 vs 0.86 (participants), 239 vs 236, 90% completed, QALY and goal-based cost-effectiveness at 2500 pounds confirmed.

494, 15 English regions, ADAS-cog difference 1.4 (0.2 to 2.6), 18.1 m exercise arm only, no secondary differences confirmed. Falls IRR 1.1 (0.8 to 1.6) and adverse events are full-text, from the record.
Intervention was progressive resistance and functional training in frail people; 'balance' not in abstract; one trial.
Exercise reduces falls by 23%; balance and functional exercises 24%; community-dwelling, specific conditions excluded.
607, 86 (14.2%), 98 on anticoagulants (16.1%), Fazekas 3 in 156 (25.7%), 320 amyloid positive (52.7%) confirmed in full text; primary care physicians recruited patients.
120 amyloid-positive pre-frail and frail, median 82, 24 (20%), 4 of 44 frail, about half under use recommendations confirmed; abstract does not state early memory problems.
7 of 16 severe (54% of 13 who reacted) vs 1 of 14 Alzheimer type; retrospective, necropsy-confirmed, 1992.
19,803 vs 61,499; 31.5 vs 18.6 per 1000 person-years; accrual 2002 to 2004; adjusted HR 1.76.
9,324, aged 65+, means 8.5 vs 9.7 and 2.1 vs 2.5, incontinence OR 0.42, authors conclude 'safer prescribing'. Mean age 84.5 is from the record.
30 studies, 1720; agitation likely not improved (moderate), depression probably slightly improved (moderate), long term no benefit (low certainty) confirmed.
1021 residents, 86 units, six countries incl. UK, 751 with 6-month data, no effect on MADRS confirmed.
69 UK homes, 847 randomised, 553 completed, d 0.24, 2.54 points, antipsychotic use not reduced confirmed; 60 minute aim is full text.
37 RCTs, 2766, MMSE 1.99, communication high quality, slight QoL and mood gains confirmed.
201 older people, 115 vs 86, MMSE p=0.044, ADAS-Cog p=0.014, QoL-AD p=0.028; 'first large' not stated.

issues.text: The difference in everyday activities was smaller than the size the researchers had set as clinically important. So the benefit is small.
issues.problem: Only the function result is set against the clinical-importance threshold, then the whole benefit is called small. The cognition difference exceeded the trial's own threshold and the authors reported cognitive benefits that exceeded the minimum clinically important difference.
issues.source_says: SMMSE higher by 1.9 points (95% CI 1.3 to 2.5; minimum clinically important difference 1.4); BADLS better by 3.0 points (95% CI 1.8 to 4.3; threshold 3.5); 'cognitive benefits that exceeded the minimum clinically important difference'.
issues.replacement: The difference in memory and thinking scores (1.9 points on a 30-point scale) was larger than the 1.4 points the researchers had set as clinically important. The difference in everyday activities (3.0 points on a 60-point scale) was smaller than their 3.5-point threshold.

issues.text: scored slightly better on memory and thinking tests and on everyday activities than those who stopped.
issues.problem: 'Slightly' understates the cognition result, which exceeded the clinically important difference; fixed by the replacement above, keep wording consistent.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: scored better on memory and thinking tests and on everyday activities than those who stopped.

issues.text: those who kept taking donepezil for a year did slightly better on cognition and daily function than those who stopped. The function difference was below the trial's own threshold for clinical importance.
issues.problem: Gives only the function result against the threshold; reader will take both differences as below threshold. Cognition difference was above it.
issues.source_says: SMMSE difference 1.9 vs threshold 1.4; BADLS difference 3.0 vs threshold 3.5.
issues.replacement: those who kept taking donepezil for a year did better on cognition and daily function than those who stopped. The cognition difference was above the trial's own threshold for clinical importance; the daily function difference was below it.

issues.text: those who kept taking it did slightly better over a year.
issues.problem: 'Slightly' understates the cognition result (above the clinical-importance threshold).
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: those who kept taking it did better over a year on thinking and daily activities.

issues.text: those who kept taking it did slightly better over a year.
issues.problem: Same as Bluesky.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: those who kept taking it did better over a year on thinking and daily activities.

issues.text: Moved to a care home within 1 year: stopped 37 in 100 / Continued 20 in 100
issues.problem: Missing 'about' (Kaplan-Meier estimates) and 'permanently'; does not name DOMINO-AD or the people studied beside the bars.
issues.source_says: Estimated probability of nursing home placement (irreversible move to a residential caring facility) within 12 months 0.37 vs 0.20; post hoc; combined arms. Abstract of Lancet Neurol 2015 confirms post hoc first-year analysis; the 0.20 and 0.37 are full-text figures.
issues.replacement: DOMINO-AD, moved permanently to a care home within 1 year: about 37 in 100 who stopped, about 20 in 100 who continued

issues.text: This came from an analysis after the trial, and the numbers are too small to be sure the drug caused it.
issues.problem: The deaths were counted in the 16-week safety follow-up; it was the statistical test of the difference that was post hoc.
issues.source_says: 'seven deaths ... by 16-week safety follow-up. Post-hoc statistical analyses suggested weak evidence of a mortality difference (Fisher's exact p=0.065)'.
issues.replacement: The deaths were counted as a safety measure; the test of the difference was done after the trial, and the numbers are too small to be sure the drug caused it.

issues.text: It came from an analysis after the trial, the numbers are small, causes of death varied, and an earlier trial of mirtazapine did not show more deaths.
issues.problem: Same post hoc imprecision; 'an earlier trial of mirtazapine' hides that it was in depression in dementia, a different condition from this trial.
issues.source_says: Earlier study was HTA-SADD, mirtazapine for depression in dementia: 108 mirtazapine vs 111 placebo, no more deaths.
issues.replacement: The test of the difference was done after the trial, the numbers are small, causes of death varied, and an earlier trial of mirtazapine for depression in dementia did not show more deaths.

issues.text: Analysis after the trial; too few deaths to be sure of cause
issues.problem: Same post hoc imprecision (the test was post hoc, not the death count).
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Difference tested after the trial; too few deaths to be sure of cause

issues.text: In US care homes, as antipsychotic use fell, use of other sedating drugs such as gabapentin and valproate rose, possibly as a substitute.
issues.problem: Maust 2018 names mood stabilisers (valproic acid and carbamazepine as examples); gabapentin is not in the opened source and 'sedating' is not the paper's term. Mood stabiliser use was already rising before the programme studied. Years not given.
issues.source_says: 'mood stabilizers [eg, valproic acid and carbamazepine]' ... 'use of mood stabilizers was growing before initiation of the partnership and then accelerated'; 'possibly as a substitute for antipsychotics'; US long-term care 2009 to 2014.
issues.replacement: In US care homes between 2009 and 2014, antipsychotic use fell while use of mood stabilisers, such as valproate and carbamazepine, rose, possibly as a substitute.

issues.text: Mirtazapine is sometimes used for agitation in dementia because it seems safer than an antipsychotic.
issues.problem: Drops 'partly': the source gives avoiding antipsychotics as one reason for the high prescribing.
issues.source_says: 'One reason for high rates of prescription of mirtazapine in later life is to avoid the use of antipsychotics.'
issues.replacement: Mirtazapine is sometimes used for agitation in dementia, partly because it seems safer than an antipsychotic.

issues.text: In the GREAT trial, 475 people with early dementia chose everyday goals and worked on them at home with a therapist.
issues.problem: Implies all 475 had therapy. About half (239) were randomised to rehabilitation and 236 to usual care. Also 'raters knew their group' is ambiguous: the researchers collecting data were blinded; the participant and family raters were not. 'Services should count goals' is a judgement not marked as one.
issues.source_says: 475 randomised (239 rehabilitation, 236 usual treatment); participant-rated outcomes; researchers blind.
issues.replacement:
GREAT trial: 475 people with early dementia were randomly assigned to home therapy on goals they chose, or usual care.

Goal ratings rose about 2.6 points vs 0.9 (raters knew the group). Quality of life, mood, memory: no clear difference.

In our view, services should count goals.

issues.text: People with early dementia in the GREAT trial each chose up to three everyday activities they wanted to manage better, and worked on them at home with a therapist.
issues.problem: Implies every participant worked with a therapist; half had usual care. Raters wording ambiguous.
issues.source_says: 475 randomised 1:1 to cognitive rehabilitation or usual treatment.
issues.replacement:
In the GREAT trial, people with early dementia each chose up to three everyday activities to manage better. About half were randomly assigned to work on them at home with a therapist; the rest had usual care.

On a 0 to 10 scale, goal ratings rose about 2.6 points with therapy, against about 0.9 with usual care. Quality of life, mood and memory scores showed no clear difference.

The raters knew their group. In our view, services should count the person's own goals too.

issues.text: Two cautions: raters knew they had had therapy, and an attentive visitor may explain some of the gain.
issues.problem: 'Raters' is ambiguous; the researchers collecting ratings were blinded, the participants and families giving them were not.
issues.source_says: Assessments by researchers blind to allocation; ratings given by participants and informants, who knew allocation.
issues.replacement: Two cautions: the people giving the ratings knew they had had therapy, and an attentive visitor may explain some of the gain.

issues.text: 475 people living at home were randomly assigned to home-based rehabilitation
issues.problem: Omits that every participant needed a family carer willing to contribute (LinkedIn has it).
issues.source_says: 'had a family carer who was willing to contribute'; people without a carer excluded.
issues.replacement: 475 people living at home, each with a family member involved, were randomly assigned to home-based rehabilitation

issues.text: In DAPA, though, falls were no different, so that benefit should not be promised to people with dementia on this evidence.
issues.problem: 'No different' reports a confidence interval that crosses the null as equivalence. Falls were carer-recalled.
issues.source_says: Falls rate ratio 1.1 (95% CI 0.8 to 1.6), no evidence of a difference.
issues.replacement: In DAPA, though, falls did not show a clear difference (the range of possible effects was wide), so that benefit should not be promised to people with dementia on this evidence.

issues.text: Falls and daily activities did not differ.
issues.problem: Non-significant result reported as no difference.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Falls and daily activities did not show a clear difference.

issues.text: A year later, their memory and thinking had not declined more slowly.
issues.problem: Outcome was at 12 months after randomisation (the 4-month programme started then); 'a year later' reads as a year after the classes. Same in LinkedIn and Bluesky ('A year on') and Threads ('A year later').
issues.source_says: ADAS-cog at 12 months after randomisation; programme 4 months.
issues.replacement: At 12 months from the start, their memory and thinking had not declined more slowly.

issues.text: Other trials show people with dementia can build strength.
issues.problem: Plural 'trials' but one small trial (Hauer 2012, 122 frail people in German outpatient geriatric rehabilitation) is the source.
issues.source_says: Hauer: 62 vs 60, 3 months progressive resistance and functional training vs low-intensity motor placebo, improved leg-press strength and chair-stand time.
issues.replacement: A German trial of frail older people with dementia found they could build strength.

issues.text: Other trials show that people with dementia can build strength. In a German trial, 3 months of strength and balance training made people stronger and quicker at standing up from a chair than a gentle comparison activity.
issues.problem: Plural 'trials' with one example; Hauer's training was progressive resistance and functional training, 'balance' is not in the abstract; population was frail people with mild to moderate dementia in outpatient rehabilitation.
issues.source_says: 'Supervised, progressive resistance and functional group training for 3 months' vs 'low-intensity motor placebo activity'; 'frail, older people with dementia'.
issues.replacement: A German trial of 122 frail older people with mild to moderate dementia found that 3 months of strength and functional training made them stronger and quicker at standing up from a chair than a gentle comparison activity.

issues.text: In our judgement, offer exercise to people with dementia for strength, getting up from a chair, and enjoyment.
issues.problem: The recommendation to offer this exercise leaves out DAPA's own harms data, and 'enjoyment' has no source (many approached declined to take part).
issues.source_says: Adverse events recorded in the exercise arm only: 23 of 329 had an exercise-related adverse event, 4 serious; 1,847 approached, 494 randomised.
issues.replacement: In DAPA, 23 of 329 people in the exercise group (about 7 in 100) had an exercise-related adverse event, and 4 had a serious one; events were recorded only in that group. In our judgement, offer exercise to people with dementia for strength and getting up from a chair, and for enjoyment if they like it.

issues.text: Fitter in class, but memory decline not slowed
issues.problem: Headline states fitness gain as fact; the authors say they cannot conclude definitively that the programme improved fitness (exercise arm only, no comparison).
issues.source_says: 'we cannot conclude definitively that the intervention improves physical fitness'.
issues.replacement: Fitness rose in class (exercise group only); memory decline not slowed

issues.text: Sources: DAPA https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.k1675 | strength training in dementia https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2011.03778.x
issues.problem: LinkedIn makes a falls claim from Sherrington et al., Cochrane 2019 that has no link.
issues.replacement: Sources: DAPA https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.k1675 | strength training in dementia https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2011.03778.x | exercise and falls https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012424.pub2

issues.text: The trial rules were stricter still. In a US study of 237 people, average age 81, with early memory problems and amyloid (a protein linked with Alzheimer's) on a brain scan, 19 (about 8 in 100) would have qualified for the trial. In a study of 44 frail older people, 4 would have.
issues.problem: 'Stricter still' presents 8 in 100 as a narrowing of the Swedish 1 in 7, but the groups differ (all presenting to primary care, about half amyloid negative, vs amyloid-positive people with mild impairment), so the figures cannot be compared. The frail figure is 4 of the 44 frail people within a study of 120, not a study of 44.
issues.source_says: Pittock: 237 MCI or mild dementia with amyloid on PET, 112 met inclusion, 19 (8%) after exclusions. Bellelli: 120 amyloid-positive pre-frail and frail adults, 24 (20%) met Clarity AD criteria, 4 of 44 frail.
issues.replacement: The trial's own rules are stricter than the criteria used in clinics. In a separate US study of 237 older people, average age 81, with early memory problems and amyloid (a protein linked with Alzheimer's) on a brain scan, 19 (about 8 in 100) would have qualified for the trial. In another study of 120 older people with amyloid, 4 of the 44 who were frail would have. These are different groups, so the figures cannot be compared with each other.

issues.text: In a study of 120 older people (median age 82) with amyloid and early memory problems, 24 (1 in 5) would have qualified for the trial.
issues.problem: The Bellelli abstract describes 120 pre-frail and frail older adults with confirmed amyloid; it does not say they had early memory problems.
issues.source_says: 'all participants with confirmed amyloid positivity (n = 120) ... pre-frail and frail older adults'; median age 82; 24 (20.0%) met Clarity-AD criteria.
issues.replacement: In a study of 120 pre-frail or frail older people (median age 82) with amyloid on testing, 24 (1 in 5) would have qualified for the trial.

issues.text: The trial rules were stricter: in a US study of 237 older people, 8 in 100 would have qualified.
issues.problem: Drops the population: it reads as 8 in 100 of older people generally. The 237 all had early memory problems and amyloid on a brain scan. 'Stricter' also compares unlike groups.
issues.source_says: 237 people with MCI or mild dementia and raised amyloid; 19 (8%) met the trial's inclusion and exclusion criteria.
issues.replacement: A separate US study applied the trial's own rules to 237 older people with early memory problems and amyloid on a brain scan. About 8 in 100 would have qualified.

issues.text: About 1 in 7 people who saw a Swedish GP with memory symptoms met the criteria for lecanemab, a new Alzheimer's drug, after full tests.
issues.problem: Omits that the denominator is everyone presenting with memory symptoms from any cause (about half were amyloid negative); without it 1 in 7 can be read as a share of people with Alzheimer's disease.
issues.source_says: 607 primary care patients with cognitive symptoms; 320 (52.7%) amyloid positive; 86 (14.2%) eligible for lecanemab.
issues.replacement: About 1 in 7 people who saw a Swedish GP with memory symptoms, whatever the cause, met the criteria for lecanemab, a new Alzheimer's drug, after full tests.

issues.text: About 1 in 7 people seeing a Swedish GP with memory symptoms met the criteria for lecanemab, an Alzheimer's drug.
issues.problem: Same missing denominator qualification ('whatever the cause') as Threads; 'after full tests' also dropped.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: About 1 in 7 people seeing a Swedish GP with memory symptoms of any cause met the criteria for lecanemab, an Alzheimer's drug, after full tests. Blood thinners and brain scan changes ruled many out.

issues.text: Trial rules are stricter than clinic rules
issues.problem: Stated on the slide whose data (237 to 112 to 19) do not show clinic rules; the support is a different study (Bellelli, same cohort, 20% vs about half). Reader will also compare 8 in 100 with the Swedish 1 in 7 on slide 1.
issues.source_says: Bellelli: 20.0% met Clarity-AD criteria vs 50.8% and 47.5% under US and French recommendations, in 120 amyloid-positive pre-frail and frail adults.
issues.replacement: In a separate study of 120 pre-frail and frail people with amyloid: 1 in 5 met the trial's rules, about half met clinic-use recommendations

issues.text: Frail older people: 4 of 44 met trial rules
issues.problem: Sits under the US 237-person funnel as if from the same sample; it is a different study (120 pre-frail and frail people with amyloid), source line names both studies together.
issues.source_says: Bellelli: 4 of 44 frail (9.1%) met Clarity-AD criteria.
issues.replacement: Separate study of 120 pre-frail and frail people with amyloid: 4 of the 44 who were frail met trial rules

issues.text: In a separate study, 4 of 44 frail older people met trial rules. Trial rules are stricter than clinic rules.
issues.problem: Alt text for slide 2 repeats the unsupported general statement and omits that the 44 are a subgroup of 120.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: In a separate study of 120 older people with amyloid, 4 of the 44 who were frail met trial rules; about half of the frail group met clinic-use recommendations.

issues.text: The ones at highest risk have Lewy body disease, and the diagnosis is often missing from the notes.
issues.problem: 'Highest risk' is a superlative across all dementias; the sources compare Lewy body with Alzheimer's disease only and say antipsychotics should be avoided 'particularly in the case of DLB'. Same sentence in LinkedIn and Threads.
issues.source_says: McKeith 2017: 'particularly in the case of DLB they should be avoided whenever possible'; McKeith 1992: severe reaction 7 of 16 Lewy body vs 1 of 14 Alzheimer type. 'Many cases missed or misdiagnosed, usually as Alzheimer disease.'
issues.replacement: The risk is particularly high in people with Lewy body disease, which is often missed or labelled as Alzheimer's disease.

issues.text: The best-known figures are old.
issues.problem: 'Best-known' is not sourced.
issues.source_says: Only the 1992 study was opened.
issues.replacement: The figures are old.

issues.text: McKeith et al., Neurology 2017; NICE NG97
issues.problem: The source line sits under 'get specialist advice first', which is house advice, not from either source.
issues.source_says: NICE 1.7.4 does not say to seek specialist advice (design note in the brief says so).
issues.replacement: Core features: McKeith et al., Neurology 2017. Antipsychotic caution: NICE NG97. Advice to ask for specialist input is ours.

issues.text: The side effects people usually hear about, and the commonest in trials, are feeling sick, vomiting and diarrhoea.
issues.problem: Evidence is from donepezil trials only; wording reads as covering all three medicines.
issues.source_says: Birks 2018: 30 donepezil trials; 'Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea were most common'.
issues.replacement: In donepezil trials, the commonest side effects were feeling sick, vomiting and diarrhoea.

issues.text: After leaving hospital, 78 of 138 people went back on the same medicine.
issues.problem: Source says they resumed cholinesterase inhibitor therapy, not necessarily the same drug.
issues.source_says: '78 of 138 cases (57%) who survived to discharge subsequently resumed cholinesterase inhibitor therapy'.
issues.replacement: After leaving hospital, 78 of 138 people went back on a medicine of the same type.

issues.text: About 81,000 older people with dementia, Canada
issues.problem: Chart data carry no timeframe; the data are from 2002 to 2004 and hospital visits are events, not people.
issues.source_says: Accrual April 2002 to March 2004; rates are events per 1000 person-years.
issues.replacement: About 81,000 older people with dementia, Ontario, Canada, 2002 to 2004

issues.text: Being given a named GP in 2014 did not make people over 75 see the same GP more often.
issues.problem: Causal verb ('make') for an observational before-and-after policy evaluation; the scheme applied to people aged over 74 (75 and over); the study actually found a small fall in the continuity score.
issues.source_says: 'The introduction of the named GP scheme was not associated with improvements in either continuity of care or rates of unplanned hospitalisation'; continuity index change -0.024.
issues.replacement: A named GP scheme for people aged 75 and over, introduced in England in 2014, was not followed by more visits to the same GP.

issues.text: One thing that did not seem to help: from 2014, people over 75 in England were given a named GP. A study found this did not increase how often they saw the same GP.
issues.problem: Same age boundary and causal wording.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: One thing that did not seem to help: from 2014, people aged 75 and over in England were given a named GP. A study found this was not followed by an increase in how often they saw the same GP.

issues.text: A named GP alone did not raise continuity in England.
issues.problem: Causal verb for observational policy evaluation; same in Bluesky ('A named GP alone did not help.') and Threads ('A named GP alone did not raise consistency.').
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: A named GP scheme was not followed by more continuity in England.

issues.text: A study of 9,324 people with dementia in England (average age 84)
issues.problem: Mean age was 84.5.
issues.source_says: mean 84.5 years (SD 7.4).
issues.replacement: A study of 9,324 people with dementia in England (average age about 85)

issues.text: (8.5 vs 9.7 on average, before adjustment). A link, not cause.
issues.problem: Compression drops that the gap was smaller after allowing for age, illness and frailty, which the other versions carry.
issues.source_says: Unadjusted means 8.52 vs 9.67; adjusted rate ratio 0.96 (0.93 to 0.98).
issues.replacement: (8.5 vs 9.7 on average; the gap was smaller after adjustment). A link, not cause.

issues.text: So ask to book with the same GP each time, and note who you saw.
issues.problem: Practical advice drawn from an association and a null policy result, not marked as judgement (also in Bluesky and Threads).
issues.source_says: Record C08-10-g: the family action is a practical suggestion, not a tested intervention.
issues.replacement: In our view, a sensible step is to ask to book with the same GP each time, and note who you saw.

issues.text: Sources: https://doi.org/10.3399/BJGP.2021.0413 | Quebec ... | 2025 editorial https://doi.org/10.3399/BJGP.2025.0199
issues.problem: LinkedIn and visual state that continuity can be counted as the share of appointments with one's own GP; that source is not linked.
issues.source_says: Sidaway-Lee et al., Br J Gen Pract 2019, DOI 10.3399/bjgp19X701813.
issues.replacement: Add: | simple measure https://doi.org/10.3399/bjgp19X701813

issues.text: Offer music for enjoyment.
issues.problem: Advice stated as fact, not marked as judgement.
issues.source_says: Record: enjoyment point is judgement.
issues.replacement: In our view, offer music for enjoyment.

issues.text: A month after sessions stopped: no benefit shown
issues.problem: Drops the qualifier that this evidence is weak (low or very low certainty), present in every caption.
issues.source_says: 'Low or very-low certainty evidence showed that music-based therapeutic interventions may not have been more effective than usual care in the long term'.
issues.replacement: A month after sessions stopped: no benefit shown (weak evidence)

issues.text: What changed in 69 nursing homes
issues.problem: Headline implies all 69 homes changed; the homes were randomised and only the programme homes (about half) received it. 'What changed' also reads as an outcome claim.
issues.source_says: Cluster randomised: 69 homes, WHELD vs treatment as usual.
issues.replacement: A care programme tested in 69 nursing homes

issues.text: 2. Social activity tailored to each resident: about an hour a week
issues.problem: States delivery as fact; the programme aimed at 60 minutes per resident per week. Threads says 'an hour a week of social activity' the same way.
issues.source_says: 'with the aim of providing 60 minutes per week per person'.
issues.replacement: 2. Social activity tailored to each resident: aiming for an hour a week

issues.text: The researchers' own view was that the planned social activity probably helped most.
issues.problem: The authors 'would speculate'; the trial cannot show which part helped.
issues.source_says: 'We would speculate that the added benefit was probably a reflection of the structured approach to promoting pleasant activities'.
issues.replacement: The researchers speculated that the planned social activity probably helped most.

issues.text: In the first large trial, 201 people with dementia took part.
issues.problem: 'First large' is not in the opened abstract.
issues.source_says: Spector 2003: 'recruited 201 older people with dementia'.
issues.replacement: In an early UK trial in 2003, 201 people with dementia took part.

issues.text: That was about 2 points on a standard memory test
issues.problem: The MMSE is a general test of thinking, not only memory.
issues.source_says: Cochrane: MMSE 1.99 points (95% CI 1.24 to 2.74), 25 studies.
issues.replacement: That was about 2 points on a 30-point test of memory and thinking
